clue.text: To me, painting is all about colour

indicators.note: all about read as 'every which way about' tells us to rearrange the preceding words

explanation.surface: An artist explains that, for them, painting is entirely a matter of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' is the anagram signal: rearrange the letters of TO ME and PAINTING; 'is' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural colouring of skin, plants or paint is called pigmentation, so the word stands for colour.

clue.text: They're ready for the Costa Brava

definitions.text: They're ready for the Costa Brava

parts.words: They're ready for the Costa Brava
parts.note: readies is British slang for cash, so these are the banknotes once spent on Spain's Costa Brava

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers are all set for a trip to the Spanish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' looks like 'prepared', but 'the ready' or 'readies' is British slang for money; the Costa Brava is in Spain, whose currency before the euro is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Spanish currency units were the money in use on the Costa Brava, a stretch of Catalan coast.

clue.text: Far from precipitate response

definitions.meaning: slow and step by step, the opposite of hasty or headlong
in the Catholic Mass, an antiphon sung or said between the readings

explanation.surface: Someone's reply is anything but hasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is liturgical: the chant sung between the Epistle and Gospel at Mass, so a churchy kind of response.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow, steady progress is the opposite of precipitate; the liturgical chant between readings bears the same name as a responsory.

clue.text: Something painted on dial of -watch detective used

parts.note: to watch is to eye, as a verb
detectives used to shadow, or tail, a suspect

explanation.surface: Something is painted onto the face of a watch a detective was using.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dial' is slang for a person's face, not a watch face; 'of' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-up applied to the lids is painted on the face, and dial is slang for face.

clue.text: Card sharp having nothing to hide

indicators.note: having here means the sour word holds the zero inside it

parts.note: a sharp taste is tart
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A card sharp has nothing to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' reads as a cheat, but 'Card' is the definition and 'sharp' the start of the wordplay; 'to hide' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Each fortune-telling card in the pack used by readers is one of these, so it is a kind of card.

clue.text: One that's behind advertisement

definitions.meaning: a vehicle towed behind a car or lorry
a short preview advertising a forthcoming film

explanation.surface: Someone lagging at the back is promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A towed cart comes behind its vehicle, and a film preview is an advert for the coming release.

clue.text: Fruit holding in stone

indicators.note: holding means the fruit word grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: an olive is a small fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit contains a stone inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fruit stone; the answer is a mineral, whose gem form is peridot.
explanation.definitionFit: This green mineral, cut as the gem peridot, is a stone in the gemmological sense.

clue.text: Spotted sequence of knock-ons that was progressively disastrous

definitions.text: Spotted sequence of knock-ons that was progressively disastrous

parts.words: Spotted sequence of knock-ons that was progressively disastrous
parts.note: a row of spotted tiles each knocking the next over, a picture of a chain reaction of calamities

explanation.surface: A chain of knock-on consequences got worse and worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' points to the dotted tiles of a game; a line of them standing on end topples one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A cumulative chain reaction is named after toppling tiles, each knocking down the next in turn.

clue.text: Performing unit including men only

indicators.note: including means the word for unit takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: one is the unit number
a stag party or night is for men only

explanation.surface: A theatre company that admits only men is putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men only' is a stag do, a British pre-wedding party for the groom and his male friends.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is in front of the audience, acting, is performing.

clue.text: Better prepared, as one gets stuck into schoolbook

indicators.note: gets stuck into means the numeral is pushed inside the book word

parts.note: a reader is a book for learning to read at school
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone becomes better prepared by getting stuck into a schoolbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'gets stuck into' looks like studying hard but puts I inside READER.
explanation.definitionFit: More ready means more prepared, the comparative of being all set.

clue.text: Couturier's success story?

parts.note: a dress designer's tale of going from poverty to wealth, with clothes as the literal joke

explanation.surface: A fashion designer tells how they made it big.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for poverty to wealth is taken literally: a couturier works in fabric, so their climb is from scraps of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes rising from poverty to great wealth, and a dressmaker literally deals in cloth.

clue.text: Maintaining contact, though dead

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby, a ball out of play over the sideline

explanation.surface: Someone keeps contact even though they have died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead' is a sporting term: in rugby and football a ball across the sideline is dead, out of play. 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping communication going is staying connected, and a ball over the sideline is out of play.

clue.text: Forceful account

definitions.meaning: striking and effective, as an argument that hits home
a narration or recounting of events

explanation.surface: A vigorous report.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking, effective point is forceful; the act of narrating a story is an account of it.

clue.text: River and lake bird

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A river and a lake are home to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is one of several English rivers of that name; the answer is an old spelling of the blackbird or ring thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the blackbird, also spelt ouzel, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Cause confusion — it's ironed out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving its three letters

explanation.surface: Someone complains that ironing has caused confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal: rearrange ITS and IRONED.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone lose their bearings is to cause confusion.

clue.text: Dump move to adopt European measure

annotationWithheld.why: Dump move to adopt European measure (9), OCR text: SCRAP and YARD account for the answer but no reading of 'move to adopt European' gives the letters, so a word looks misread and no source gives the printed clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Dump move to adopt European measure

clue.text: All available force needed to dismiss authority

parts.note: to dismiss from a job is to fire
authority is power

explanation.surface: Every bit of strength is needed to remove someone from office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed to' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The total weaponry a force can bring to bear, or figuratively all available strength.

clue.text: Person finding new place to hear poetry reader

indicators.note: to hear means the coined word is spoken out loud

parts.note: one who re-sites, moving something to a new site

explanation.surface: Someone finds a new venue for listening to a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A re-siter, coined for someone who finds a new site, said out loud is a declaimer of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reads verse aloud from memory before an audience is a poetry reader.

clue.text: Theatre put up with variety act

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word for theatre is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rep is short for a repertory theatre
a form is a kind or variety

explanation.surface: A theatre stages a variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns REP into PER; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on stage is to give a show, a synonym in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Henry's captain providing grand final section for 16

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: final section for 16 asks for the closing letters of that entry, dropping its opening ones

parts.note: 16 refers to the answer at 16 across

explanation.surface: A captain from a Shakespeare history brings the last part of the force.
explanation.walkthrough: Gower is a Welsh-front captain in Shakespeare's Henry V; the closing four letters, OWER, of the 16-across answer follow G. 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's history play about the fifth king of that name, the English officer of this name is one of his captains.

clue.text: Impressive area round a European city

indicators.note: round means the word for impressive goes around the single letter

parts.note: grand means impressive

explanation.surface: An impressive district surrounds a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts GRAND around A, giving GRANAD, and A for area follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andalusian city of the Alhambra is in Spain, so a European city.

clue.text: Rebel crossing southern border, as some jokingly say

definitions.text: southern border, as some jokingly say

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
a ford is a river crossing

explanation.surface: A rebel crosses the southern frontier, as some joke.
explanation.walkthrough: A town just north of London; Londoners joke that anywhere 'north of' it is the North, so it marks the edge of the South.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hertfordshire town is jokingly treated as the frontier between the soft South and the North of England.

clue.text: Bit of work goalkeeper finally put in to save

indicators.note: put in means the final letter is slipped inside the word for save

parts.note: save, as in all save one, means except

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of goalkeeper

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper finally gets in position to make a save.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' is the preposition 'but', not a goalkeeper's stop; R, the last letter of goalkeeper, goes inside EXCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage taken from a book or piece of music is an extract, a bit of the work.

clue.text: News organisation burdened with a thousand things to do

indicators.note: burdened with means the agency's name carries the letter inside it

parts.note: TASS was the Soviet news agency
K is short for a thousand

explanation.surface: A news agency is loaded with a thousand jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: TASS, the Soviet and now Russian state news agency, takes K for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs or chores on a list are things to do.

clue.text: Such surgery paid for by 'credit card?

definitions.meaning: cosmetic or reconstructive surgery of this name
a credit card is slang for money in card form, so paying on card

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery is settled on a credit card.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word names reconstructive surgery and, informally, credit cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconstructive surgery bears this name, and credit cards are colloquially called it after their material.

clue.text: Colours designed for some men to carry in military displays

definitions.text: Colours designed for some men to carry
definitions.meaning: inked designs on the skin, which men bear about with them
evening shows of military music and drill, like the one at Edinburgh

explanation.surface: Regimental colours are made for soldiers to carry in military parades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colours' looks like regimental flags, but means inked skin designs; the military sense is a show like the Edinburgh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked skin designs are coloured pictures men carry; a military pageant of drill and music shares the name.

clue.text: A lot of rot found in seafood

indicators.note: lot of means most of the word, the last letter dropped

parts.note: baloney means nonsense or rot

explanation.surface: Plenty of rot is found in some seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot of' trims the Y off BALONEY; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible sea snail, also called ormer, is eaten as a shellfish delicacy.

clue.text: What Lenin did 'for the peasants was heaven

definitions.meaning: the Bolsheviks pledged 'peace, bread and land', offering peasants farmland
the place of everlasting bliss, a paradise

explanation.surface: Lenin's offer to the peasants was paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Lenin's slogan 'Peace, Land and Bread' promised land; the Biblical phrase for Canaan also means paradise. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical Canaan pledged to Abraham's descendants has come to mean any paradise or heaven.
